note: The shared artifact. scripts/peer/publication.mjs is a worked example and Starcom's TypeScript is another; neither is authoritative. Port the policy or write your own, then check it here. Agreeing on outcomes while disagreeing about implementation is what lets nodes cooperate without one being in charge.

vectors.name: contained-by-default
vectors.description: Material held in a workspace is not a publication candidate, whatever else is true.

vectors.name: contained-outranks-consent
vectors.description: Containment is checked ABOVE consent — a released decision is separate from a publish decision.

vectors.name: released-then-judged
vectors.description: Released material still faces every check below it. Release is not permission.

vectors.name: absent-containment-passes
vectors.description: Absent containment means NOT containment-managed, and does not block. Opt-in, not universal.

vectors.name: fabricated-refused
vectors.description: Mock evidence never reaches the wire, signed and indistinguishable from real intelligence.

vectors.name: unmeasured-provenance-refused
vectors.description: Undefined is refused alongside true: "nobody said" is not permission.

vectors.name: organization-publishes
vectors.description: Institutions are accountable. This is the ordinary case and must not prompt.

vectors.name: object-publishes
vectors.description: Threat infrastructure, vessels, hashes. Nothing here touches a person.

vectors.name: place-publishes
vectors.description: A location where something regulated happened.

vectors.name: unknown-subject-publishes
vectors.description: Deliberately allowed. Blocking it would make the person prompt routine, and a prompt that appears constantly stops being deliberation.

vectors.name: public-office-with-consent
vectors.description: A legislator taking money from the regulator they chair. The least controversial publication in journalism.

vectors.name: public-office-without-consent
vectors.description: Publishable, but still deliberate. Consent keeps it an act rather than a side effect.

vectors.name: corporate-officer
vectors.description: A named officer acting in a role they hold publicly and are accountable for.

vectors.name: criminal-persona
vectors.description: A threat actor handle attributed by its own conduct. Core cyber investigation work.

vectors.name: private-consent-alone-refused
vectors.description: THE LOAD-BEARING CASE. Consent alone published a whistleblower identity, a child's home address, a private donor and a recruitment candidate.

vectors.name: private-absent-role-is-private
vectors.description: No subjectRole means private. Defaulting the other way would publish anyone nobody classified.

vectors.name: private-with-justification
vectors.description: No absolute bar, deliberately: absolute bars get routed around. A landlord with 214 unremedied violations publishes because someone wrote down why.

vectors.name: private-justification-without-consent
vectors.description: Both are required. A stated reason does not replace the decision to publish.

vectors.name: private-blank-justification
vectors.description: Whitespace is not a justification. An empty field would let the check be satisfied by pressing a key.

vectors.name: unrecognised-role-refused
vectors.description: An unknown role is refused rather than coerced to private — a typo must not silently change the decision.
